scope: Read-only existing OSS maintenance, managed update, rollback and repair chain; no broad tests or changes

generalExistingMechanisms.capability: Durable single-dispatch receipt, exact local image IDs/configuration, unchanged mount/data/service declarations and optional trusted behavior verification.
Existing release application invokes one baseline recovery on caught update failure when a trusted verifier and receipt exist; fresh readiness authorization still required.

Recovery validates original/candidate/current images, retained mounts and baseline behavior; uncertain original dispatch or recovery dispatch cannot be replayed. Explicit negative behavior is distinct from unknown verifier failure.
Retained receipt reconciliation and completed-release behavior inspection through existing status/review-status calls; no duplicate application.
Existing source-bound real-error -> native builder -> separate oracle -> comparison/review -> managed application -> installed behavior proof route; historical example remains blocked at oracle.

hardcodedBoundaries.restriction: Owner policy requires exactly psycopg+psycopg-binary and target3.3.6; sensory selectors and completion text also hardcode psycopg3.3.4->3.3.6.
Fixed package pair/version, official version-specific URLs and required installed baseline3.3.4. No general newest-compatible-release discovery or second update cycle.
cp312/x86_64/glibcwheel selection, pair-specific metadata rewrite/build/recovery and driver behavior checks. Generic structure exists, but acceptance is driver-specific.
Only existing core and delegated-work-worker images may change. Data services, inventory, mounts/configuration/migrations are rejected by this image-only updater.

findings.title: Known dependency behavior failures do not reach explicit-negative rollback contract
evidence: runtime_dependency_update.py588-597 raises ValueError for completed driver test output mismatch and failed interface conditions. Verifier returns only verifiedTrue.
runtime_image_update.py297-307 deliberately treats verifier exceptions as unknown observations and returns without compensation.
component_application_runtime.py639-649 therefore cannot guarantee rollback of these dependency behavior regressions despite calling recovery.
findings.nextStep: Return typed verifiedFalse with bounded failure evidence for completed, authenticated behavioral failures. Continue raising for incomplete execution, source/image tampering or unknown infrastructure. Prove one guarded compensation and baseline readback in existing isolated recovery fixture.

findings.title: Later behavior inspection is caller-triggered, not an autonomous watch
evidence: reviewed_component_application.py359-377 invokes inspect only when review_status/status is called.
Queue dispatch loop470-489 selects queued/waiting jobs only. Completed jobs have no periodic inspection schedule.
RuntimeRepairDevelopment excludes completed jobs from pending; MaintenanceStages.observe_due polls fixed software inventory/releases, not completed release behavior.
findings.nextStep: Use one bounded due-check in existing controller for the currently installed exact reviewed candidate, sharing existing queue inspection and readiness guards. Do not reopen historical jobs or run external actions as probes.

findings.title: Update failure/recovery evidence is not directly linked to Eva cause-analysis goal
evidence: Dependency maintenance application recoveries become baseline_retained; exceptions become retained blocked/unconfirmed handoff state.

No maintenance/update recovery callback directly observes a source-correlated SELF_REPAIR incident. Existing core error observer can independently create incidents, but causal update receipt linkage/later repair is not demonstrated.
findings.nextStep: Feed exact candidate/baseline/recovery receipt hashes and bounded verified failure category into existing self-repair intake once, with original owner/source/STOP constraints; unknown effects remain uncertain.

smallestGeneralizationAfterRollbackVerdi.change: Replace fixed PAIR/VERSION and baseline literals with one immutable host-owned dependency target descriptor consumed by existing policy, InstalledDependencyTarget and MaintenanceStages.
descriptorBinds: official registry/release artifact hashes and dependency resolution
fixed independent compatibility/original-behavior and baseline-recovery references
smallestGeneralizationAfterRollbackVerdi.firstAdditionalTarget: PydanticAI/OpenAI/httpx2 pinned compatible set already investigated in isolation; do not pip-upgrade installed services or admit arbitrary model-selected shell commands.
smallestGeneralizationAfterRollbackVerdi.reuse: Existing builder, oracle/reviewer authority, publisher, application queue, image updater and self-repair; no new platform.
smallestGeneralizationAfterRollbackVerdi.coverageLimit: Current inventory includes core/worker Python distributions and declared image/provider/extension metadata. It does not establish exhaustive OS/npm/host/database/model-backend version coverage.

preservedSafety: No database snapshot rollback or data rewind; retain current volumes and all historical failure evidence.
Schema migrations/stateful service upgrades require separate explicit compatible forward/recovery contracts.
Require actual current work/assessment/lease/STOP checks immediately before application/recovery; no age-based waiver.
Unknown inspections and effects never become proven failures or replay authorization.
No private prompts, credentials or hidden criteria exposed.
limitations: Source-based findings, no new runtime update/recovery trial.
Generic allOSS autonomous updating, later regression detection and Eva repair/reuse are not proven or technically complete.
